integrations.delete_gitlab_instance_confirm_msg_one: This removes the GitLab instance and its 1 watched repository (revoking webhooks where possible). Past analyses remain visible.

integrations.telegram_webhook_failed: We could not register Telegram's webhook automatically - you can still finish /link, but the connection may be flaky. Double-check TELEGRAM public_base_url.

onboarding.subtitle: Three minutes to your first AI root cause.
onboarding.track_title: How would you like to connect?
onboarding.track_subtitle: Pick the path that matches your setup. You can always add the other one later from Settings → Integrations.
onboarding.track_git_desc: GitLab, GitHub, or Bitbucket. We sign in via OAuth (or you paste a webhook URL) and watch your repositories automatically.
onboarding.track_api_desc: For Jenkins, CircleCI, TeamCity, Drone, GitHub Actions / GitLab CI without OAuth, or any custom pipeline. Issue an API token and POST failure logs from your pipeline.
onboarding.track_api_b1: Works with strict security policies (no OAuth required)
onboarding.track_api_b2: One curl per pipeline failure — language and stack agnostic
onboarding.track_api_b3: Free tier supports 3 active API keys
onboarding.track_api_disabled: API tokens aren't available on this plan. Upgrade to Startup or higher to issue API keys.
onboarding.ci_pick_subtitle: We'll tailor the quickstart snippet for the system you choose. You can also add more later from Settings.

ci_desc.teamcity: JetBrains TeamCity build steps with on-failure script.
ci_desc.drone: Drone CI or Woodpecker on any runner.
ci_desc.github_actions: Use this if your plan doesn't support GitHub OAuth or you prefer keeping it manual.
ci_desc.gitlab_ci: Use this if your plan doesn't support GitLab OAuth or you prefer keeping it manual.
ci_desc.generic: Anything else: Buildkite, Concourse, Argo, Bamboo, Tekton, scripts on a VM…

onboarding.token_subtitle: We'll create a bearer token scoped to log ingestion. The raw secret is shown only once — store it in your CI's secret manager.
onboarding.quickstart_subtitle: Paste the snippet into your pipeline config. Run any failing build to verify — the analysis will appear in your dashboard within seconds.
onboarding.quickstart_missing_token: Token is missing — go back and create one before continuing.
onboarding.quickstart_git_upsell_title: Want PR comments and inline checks too?
onboarding.quickstart_git_upsell_desc: If your repository lives on GitLab, GitHub, or Bitbucket, you can additionally connect the Git host so Exlogare posts the AI root cause directly into pull/merge requests and commits.
onboarding.api_messenger_upsell_hint: Free includes API ingest + dashboard. Telegram / Slack / Matrix notifications are part of Startup and above.
onboarding.provider_subtitle: Pick GitLab CI, GitHub Actions, or Bitbucket Pipelines. You can add more connections later in Integrations.
onboarding.provider_gitlab_desc: Pipelines, merge requests, and GitLab-style feedback.
onboarding.provider_github_desc: Workflows, pull requests, and issue-style feedback on github.com or GitHub Enterprise.
onboarding.provider_bitbucket_desc: Pipelines, pull requests, and commit comments on Bitbucket Cloud or Data Center.
onboarding.provider_gitflic_desc: Russian Git hosting with built-in CI/CD. Supports gitflic.ru cloud and self-hosted instances.
onboarding.connect_oauth_cloud_intro: You're about to be redirected to {{provider}} and asked to approve access. The browser will bounce you back to Exlogare in a few seconds — no copy-pasting tokens, no password stored on our side.
onboarding.connect_oauth_step1_desc: Opens the provider's sign-in page. If you're already signed in there, you'll jump straight to the consent screen.
onboarding.connect_oauth_step2_desc_gitlab: We request api, read_user, read_repository — needed to read failed pipelines, auto-register the webhook, and post RCA to merge requests. Only the access/refresh token is stored; your password never reaches us.
onboarding.connect_oauth_step2_desc_github: We request repo, read:user, workflow, and admin:repo_hook — needed to read GitHub Actions logs, auto-register the webhook, and comment on pull requests.
onboarding.connect_oauth_step2_desc_gitflic: We request PROJECT_READ, PROJECT_WRITE, PROJECT_EDIT, USER_READ — needed to list projects, read failed pipelines, and register the PIPELINE_FAIL webhook.
onboarding.connect_oauth_step3_desc: Next step you pick which repositories to watch. The failure webhook is registered automatically.
onboarding.connect_oauth_revoke_gitlab: GitLab: User Settings → Applications → Authorized applications. Or delete the connection from Exlogare → Integrations.
onboarding.connect_oauth_revoke_github: GitHub: Settings → Applications → Authorized OAuth Apps. Or delete the connection from Exlogare → Integrations.
onboarding.connect_oauth_revoke_gitflic: GitFlic: Profile Settings → Oauth Applications → Access. Or delete the connection from Exlogare → Integrations.
onboarding.messenger_gated_title: Chat notifications are a paid-plan feature
onboarding.messenger_gated_subtitle: On Free, RCA lands in the dashboard and email. Telegram / Slack / Matrix / Mattermost / Discord / MS Teams unlock on Startup and above.
onboarding.messenger_where_to_see_title: Where you'll see results right now
onboarding.messenger_where_dashboard: On the dashboard home — a live list of recent failed pipelines with root cause and fix suggestion.
onboarding.messenger_where_analyses: In the Analyses section — full RCA history per project, with filters and search.
onboarding.messenger_where_email: Daily digest by email, if notifications are enabled in your profile settings.
onboarding.messenger_upgrade_title: What you'll add on a paid plan
onboarding.messenger_upgrade_desc: Notifications hit your chat within seconds of a failure — the team doesn't wait for someone to refresh the dashboard.
onboarding.messenger_upgrade_b1: Telegram bot: DM or group chat, with a deep link to the pipeline.
onboarding.messenger_upgrade_b2: Slack / Mattermost / Discord / MS Teams via incoming webhook.
onboarding.messenger_upgrade_b3: Matrix — for teams on self-hosted Synapse / Element.
onboarding.flavor_saas_gitflic_desc: Russian-hosted GitFlic cloud — one-click OAuth using the operator-configured OAuth application.
onboarding.flavor_self_gitflic_desc: Your own GitFlic instance — provide a base URL and client_id/secret from your OAuth application.
onboarding.flavor_saas_bitbucket_desc: Atlassian's hosted Bitbucket — one-click OAuth when your operator configured an OAuth Consumer.
onboarding.flavor_self_bitbucket_desc: Self-hosted Bitbucket — webhook-only with an optional Personal Access Token for auto-registration.
onboarding.bitbucket_dc_webhook_only_hint: Bitbucket Data Center is webhook-only — paste the project key and repo slug; we'll register the hook if you supply a Personal Access Token, otherwise we'll show copy-paste instructions.
onboarding.bitbucket_cloud_oauth_only_hint: Bitbucket Cloud uses OAuth in this wizard. Webhook-only mode is available from Integrations after onboarding for Data Center installations.
onboarding.dc_legacy_warning_bitbucket: Bitbucket Data Center 7.4 or newer is required for the 'Build status updated' webhook event. On older versions, RCAs can still run via POST /api/analyze for manual ingestion.
onboarding.connect_oauth_self_hint_bitbucket: Bitbucket Cloud uses Atlassian OAuth — your operator registers the OAuth Consumer once for the whole tenancy. There is no per-customer OAuth in this wizard.
onboarding.connect_oauth_scopes_hint_bitbucket: Required scopes: repository, pullrequest:write, webhook, pipeline, account.
onboarding.bitbucket_oauth_scope_error: Bitbucket refused the authorization because the OAuth Consumer is missing required scopes. Open Workspace settings → OAuth consumers, edit the consumer, and tick: Account: Read, Pull requests: Write, Repositories: Read, Webhooks: Read and write, Pipelines: Read. Save and try again.
onboarding.projects_empty_bitbucket: No repositories returned. Make sure your Bitbucket account has access to a workspace and that the OAuth Consumer has the required scopes.
onboarding.flavor_saas_github_desc: The public service — one-click OAuth when your operator configured a platform app.
onboarding.flavor_self_github_desc: Your own host — create an OAuth App and paste Application ID and Secret in the next step.
onboarding.github_oauth_only_hint: GitHub Actions in this wizard uses OAuth (PAT and webhook-only flows are available from Integrations after you finish onboarding if your plan allows them).
onboarding.flavor_saas_desc: The public hosted GitLab - one-click OAuth.
onboarding.flavor_self_desc: Your own instance - bring your own OAuth app or use Webhook-only.
onboarding.connect_oauth_self_hint: For self-hosted GitLab, register an Application in your instance (Admin Area or your user profile) with redirect URL
onboarding.connect_oauth_self_hint_github: For GitHub Enterprise, register an OAuth App with redirect URL
onboarding.connect_oauth_scopes_hint: Use scopes that allow API access, typically api and read_user (some GitLab versions show read_api).
onboarding.connect_oauth_scopes_hint_github: Use a scope that allows reading repos and writing feedback — typically `repo` (private repos) and `read:user` for the OAuth app.
onboarding.watch_mode_unavailable: Could not determine an allowed integration mode for your plan. Reload the page or try again in a moment.
onboarding.connect_webhook_intro: Paste the project URL or group/project slug. If you also paste a Personal Access Token (api scope), we will register the webhook automatically. Otherwise we'll give you copy-paste instructions.
onboarding.projects_empty: No projects returned. You may need more permissions on the GitLab account.
onboarding.projects_empty_github: No repositories returned. Grant `repo` on the token or check organization access for the GitHub account.
onboarding.finish_webhook_setup: Finish the webhook setup in GitLab
onboarding.messenger_subtitle: Pick at least one channel to receive AI RCAs. You can add more later.
onboarding.telegram_code_hint: Code expires in 30 minutes. Your messages will arrive here as soon as we get it.
onboarding.slack_connected: Connected - we sent a test message.
onboarding.telegram_connected: Telegram webhook registered - send the /link code to finish.
onboarding.demo_intro: We'll run the full AI pipeline on a realistic CI failure. If you connected a messenger, the summary will arrive there in a moment.

settings.title: Settings
settings.subtitle: Team identity, privacy and audit log. Integrations, messengers, API keys and webhooks live under Integrations.
settings.team_desc: How your team appears across dashboards and notifications.
settings.team_members_desc: Invite teammates and manage their roles. Owners and admins can change settings; members can only view.
settings.remove_member_msg: They will lose access to all dashboards and integrations.
settings.audit_log_desc: Read-only timeline of admin events: token creation/revocation, integration changes, plan switches, payment events. Retained per your plan's history retention.
settings.privacy_desc: Exlogare publishes a quarterly aggregated "State of CI Failures" report. Only failures seen by at least 5 distinct teams ever appear, and we never include team / project / repo identifiers. Toggle off to exclude this team from the aggregation set.
settings.api_tokens_desc: Bearer credentials for the universal CI ingest endpoints (Jenkins, CircleCI, TeamCity, Drone, GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, generic). Raw secrets are shown only once at creation.
settings.api_tokens_limit_reached: Token limit reached on this plan. Revoke an existing one or upgrade.
settings.revoke_token_msg: Clients using this token will start seeing 401 immediately.
settings.token_created_warn: This is the only time we will show this secret. Copy it into your secret manager before closing the dialog.
settings.feedback_desc: Where Exlogare posts the AI root-cause analysis when a pipeline fails — applies to GitLab, GitHub and Bitbucket alike. Turning a channel off here disables it for every project in this team (kill switch). Individual projects may further narrow these defaults under Integrations.
settings.feedback_mr_comment_hint: Posts the RCA as a note on the open PR (GitHub / Bitbucket) or MR (GitLab) tied to the failing pipeline.
settings.feedback_commit_comment_hint: Fallback when no PR/MR is available: adds the RCA as a commit comment on the failing SHA.
settings.feedback_issue_hint: Last-resort fallback for pipelines with neither an MR/PR nor a commit context (e.g. scheduled runs). Currently supported on GitLab.
settings.feedback_kill_switch: Disabling a channel here overrides any per-project override: it will be OFF everywhere.
settings.quickstart_read_hint: Read API requires scope=read on the token.
settings.notif_upsell_title: Want Slack/Telegram alerts on every analysis?
settings.notif_upsell_desc: Free includes API ingest + dashboard RCA. Notifications are part of Startup and above.
settings.feedback_status_check_hint: GitHub: posts a Check Run with severity-aware conclusion. Bitbucket: posts a Build Status keyed exlogare/rca. Both surfaces deep-link to the analysis on Exlogare. Fires alongside (not instead of) the comment cascade and is best-effort: a 4xx from the host doesn't stop the comment from landing.
